# Harnesses that get a SHARD TO THEMSELVES in .github/workflows/kani-full.yml.
#
# Rule: anything measured at >= 600 s solo. On a GitHub hosted runner (slower than
# the box those numbers came from) that is already >= ~20 min, and letting the
# bin-packer put two of them together is how a shard ends up near the 6 h job
# ceiling for a reason that has nothing to do with a regression.
#
# The packer assigns these in file order, one per shard, starting at shard 1, then
# LPT-packs everything else into the remaining shards. If this file ever grows
# past the shard count the packer falls back to packing everything, so adding a
# name here can never silently drop a harness from the sweep.
#
# name                                                              solo wall (2026-08-24)
proof_v16_terminal_realization_floored_rate_pays_zero_and_moves_nothing
# ^ MEASURED ON A RUNNER: 410 s, SUCCESSFUL, 2 of 2 covers, 0 of 8181 checks failed
#   (run 34944024488, job 104299114509). It keeps its own shard because the two
#   pre-runner figures for it were both wrong in interesting ways: the 1800 s
#   "solo" number was the 2026-08-24 run's TIMEOUT CAP (a lower bound that was never
#   a measurement) and the 3710 s at 22440ebb was contention. 410 s is the real cost.
proof_v16_expired_backing_yields_zero_realizable_support_after_expiry
# ^ 799 s solo; 7093 s on a loaded box. Also in hosted_runner_excluded.tsv: it KILLS
#   a hosted runner, so the planner routes it to shard 0 and this entry never applies.
#   Kept here so the entry survives a move to a larger runner.
proof_v17_wide_mul_div_floor_stub_correct
# ^ 736 s solo. Note the near-name trap: proof_v17_wide_mul_div_floor_postcondition_u16
#   is written inside a DOC COMMENT in tests/proofs_v17_fork.rs and is not a harness
#   at all; this one is real.
